body:
## What to build

Keep the complete requested SQLite table identifier throughout direct materialization of a Margin result. Computing into an attached database must populate that database's table and leave an existing same-named table in another schema unchanged.

This is a silent write to the wrong destination, not only an incorrect returned result. Treat it as the highest-priority fix in this investigation.

## Reproduction and observed behavior

Confirmed on unmodified [6a5f611](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/commit/6a5f611d41bd462f3c933edea1dd0b9861d6e892), installed in an isolated library and exercised from fresh R processes without testthat. R 4.6.1, dplyr 1.2.1, dbplyr 2.6.0, DBI 1.3.0, RSQLite 3.53.3. All data and databases were synthetic.

1. Open an in-memory SQLite connection and attach a second in-memory database as `other`.
2. Copy a two-row tibble to `source`: character `g = c("a", "b")`, double `v = c(2, 5)`.
3. Create persistent `main.report` containing exactly one sentinel row: `g = "keep"`, integer `id = 99L`, double `total = -1`.
4. Call `summarize_with_margins()` on `source` with `total = sum(v, na.rm = TRUE)`, `.grouping = rollup(g)`, and `.id = "id"`. Leave the label and sort defaults unchanged.
5. Call `compute()` on that result with `name = dbplyr::in_schema("other", "report")`, `temporary = FALSE`, and `analyze = FALSE`.
6. Collect the returned table and read `main.report` independently through DBI.

Expected: `other.report` contains `(a, 1L, 2)`, `(b, 1L, 5)`, `(Total, 2L, 7)`. The sentinel is the only row in `main.report`.

Actual: materialization succeeds without a warning, `other.report` is empty, and those three result rows are appended to `main.report` (one row becomes four).

An independent investigator reproduced the write using a different three-row fixture and an ordinary SQL aggregation control. `DBI::Id(schema = "other", table = "report")` also reproduces it. Ordinary dbplyr materialization preserves the destination and sentinel. With no competing table name, the Margin operation succeeds correctly. Qualified names with `temporary = TRUE` are refused by ordinary SQLite too and are outside this defect.

## Contract, diagnosis, and history

[ADR 0031](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/6a5f611d41bd462f3c933edea1dd0b9861d6e892/design/adr/0031-preserve-sqlite-typed-dimensions-under-margin-order.md) promises materialization into the requested table while retaining ordinary naming behavior.

The observed defect is in [the SQLite materialization method](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/6a5f611d41bd462f3c933edea1dd0b9861d6e892/R/sqlite-typed-order.R), `compute.marginplyr_sqlite_typed_result()`. It creates the qualified destination, then obtains a bare name with `remote_name()` for INSERT and ANALYZE. A different schema can therefore win SQLite's name resolution. Preserve the complete identifier rather than treating the destination as a bare string.

Same-dependency comparison: before #640 / #650 (`ad851dbefe99cf1cf6987dc5f0716f6a13d3873b`) both sorted typed and unsorted `.id` cases succeeded. Before #653 (`d4ea5f09d5698a6a89b68ecfd62ad450a4089bba`), the sorted typed case failed but the unsorted `.id` case succeeded. The investigated head fails both. #653 / #658 expanded the affected dedicated path; it did not introduce the original sorted-path defect.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both `in_schema()` and `DBI::Id()` materialize into the fully qualified persistent destination when another schema contains a same-named, compatible table. Assert exact result values and that the other table remains unchanged.
- [ ] Cover sorted typed-label results and ordinary unsorted results using `.id`; preserve public column names, declared types, row count, and promised Margin order.
- [ ] Preserve ordinary destination overwrite/index/analyze behavior. Follow-up statements must address the same qualified destination as table creation, including when analysis is enabled.
- [ ] Failure leaves unrelated tables untouched and cleans up internal temporary resources. Retain the existing atomic materialization protections.
- [ ] Add public-API regressions with independent DBI observations of both schemas. Preserve lazy construction's query policy and run the required package checks.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately). Other defects in the dedicated SQLite materialization method are independent; overlapping edits require coordination, not a prerequisite fix.
title: Preserve schema-qualified destinations when materializing SQLite Margin results
